description.en: The aim of the experiment is to verify Thevenin's Theorem by determining the Thevenin equivalent voltage (VTH) and equivalent resistance (RTH), and calculating the load current through the load resistance.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
To use this feature, click on the AI Guide button. The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.
The AUTO CONNECT button automatically creates all the required circuit connections for the experiment.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.

Note: If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding terminal label number to remove the connection.
The ADD button records the measured values of VTH, RTH, RL and IL in the observation table.

The CALCULATE button computes the Thevenin equivalent voltage (VTH), equivalent resistance (RTH), and the theoretical load current (IL). Enter the calculated IL value and click VERIFY to compare it with the observed value.
The RESET button refreshes the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.
Set the values of R1, R2, R3 and RL using the resistance sliders. These resistance values are used to determine the Thevenin equivalent circuit.
The voltmeter measures the Thevenin equivalent voltage (VTH), the ammeter measures the load current (IL), and the digital multimeter measures the Thevenin equivalent resistance (RTH).
This section provides the required DC voltage to the circuit. The display shows the applied source voltage, and the slider can be used to set the desired voltage.
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections by dragging and dropping wires between the connection points.
This table records the measured values of VTH, RTH, RL and IL. These readings are used later for calculation and verification.
This section displays the equations used to calculate the Thevenin equivalent voltage, equivalent resistance and load current.
This panel displays VTH, RTH and RL, and allows you to verify the manually calculated load current using the formula IL = VTH / (RTH + RL).

The REPORT button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observations and verification, generate the report. The report includes the experiment summary, measured readings, calculations, verification result and conclusion.
